original_question: Is there a finite non-abelian group G of odd order, with k(G) conjugacy classes, such that k(G)/|G| = 1/17?
target_in_paper: 20th Issue (2022), Problem 20.52: the Burnside-motivated realization problem asking whether every positive multiple of 16 occurs as |G|-k(G) for some finite non-abelian group of odd order. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the setting of finite non-abelian groups of odd order and uses k(G) in the sense of counting conjugacy classes. Those are the key objects in the paper's nearest matching problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's official question is not about the single ratio k(G)/|G|=1/17; instead it asks for every integer m>0. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
The defining condition in the paper is |G(m)|-k(G(m))=16m, not a fixed proportionality between k(G) and |G|. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
The paper explicitly states that k(G) denotes the number of conjugacy classes of a finite group G; a stand-alone version should say this directly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

The group is allowed to depend on m and is written as G(m); the quantifier structure is: for every positive integer m, there exists such a finite non-abelian odd-order group. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

Burnside's divisibility statement is part of the official formulation: if G has odd order, then |G|-k(G) is divisible by 16. This is the paper's motivation for the realization problem and should be retained. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Let k(G) denote the number of conjugacy classes of a finite group G. Burnside proved that if G has odd order, then |G|-k(G) is divisible by 16. Is it true that for every positive integer m there exists a finite non-abelian group G(m) of odd order such that |G(m)|-k(G(m))=16m? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
justification: The nearest paper-faithful target is Problem 20.52. Your draft matches the paper in focusing on finite non-abelian odd-order groups and conjugacy-class counts, but it replaces the paper's actual universal realization problem by the much narrower and different condition k(G)/|G|=1/17. This arXiv item is the Kourovka Notebook, organized by numbered problems rather than by Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3; within it, the exact official formulation closest to your draft is the Burnside-based question in Problem 20.52. The adjacent Problem 20.51 concerns prescribing the exact number of conjugacy classes t, but it does not involve the divisibility-by-16 condition, so 20.52 is the correct target. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300))
